PERF-001.rationale: The provider invokes the pinned real Lighthouse engine through the trusted browser capability.

PERF-002.rationale: Purpose is explicit and the provided suite declares separate nodes.

PERF-003.rationale: The schema does not permit accessibility as a Lighthouse purpose; Axe owns it.

PERF-004.rationale: The provider defaults performance to three runs.

PERF-005.rationale: The strict schema permits five performance runs.

PERF-006.rationale: The capability awaits each real Lighthouse run in a single loop.

PERF-007.rationale: The provider calculates route medians from all performance reports.

PERF-008.rationale: The schema fixes SEO and best-practices to one run.

PERF-009.rationale: Every real run creates a separate Lighthouse report evidence file.

PERF-010.rationale: One median-score report per route is marked representative.

PERF-011.rationale: The provider resolves a reviewed named profile from the project settings file.

PERF-012.rationale: The capability validates bounded device, network, CPU, and screen settings; operator policy owns execution ceilings.

PERF-013.rationale: Provider details and each capability result name the profile.

PERF-014.rationale: Provider details record Lighthouse and browser versions from real reports.

PERF-015.rationale: Provider details record worker limits and benchmark index.

PERF-016.rationale: Performance nodes select one named combined budget.

PERF-017.rationale: A minimum performance score creates a blocking failed check.

PERF-018.rationale: Named budgets enforce maximum LCP, CLS, and TBT values.

PERF-019.rationale: The provider applies every defined budget value to each route.

PERF-020.rationale: Advisory performance can run without a budget and report evidence; blocking performance must select a reviewed budget.

PERF-021.rationale: SEO and best-practices results retain their category scores.

PERF-022.rationale: Every applicable failed category audit becomes a visible finding.

PERF-023.rationale: Acceptances require exact audit, route, useful reason, and valid expiry fields.

PERF-024.rationale: Budget and unaccepted audit failures return a failed provider result.

PERF-025.rationale: A real external subresource request is denied by the exact-origin proxy.

PERF-DEFECT-026.rationale: The direct CLI suite, mixed accessibility category, flat thresholds, and old report authority are deleted.

PERF-027.rationale: Typed fixture origins replace implicit localhost port selection.

PERF-028.rationale: The provided suite and examples retain the root route default explicitly.

PERF-029.rationale: A strict bounded node timeout replaces the implicit 60 second value.

PERF-030.rationale: The plan and capability deadlines remain bounded by operator policy.

PERF-031.rationale: Cancellation kills Chrome and closes the exact-origin proxy.

PERF-032.rationale: The isolated provider runner and dedicated Chrome launch replace an inherited suite subprocess environment.

PERF-033.rationale: The real provider test proves a blocking score or metric budget failure.

PERF-034.rationale: Missing required categories and metrics are explicit execution errors.

PERF-035.rationale: Advisory nodes preserve complete reports and category failures without blocking the gate.

PERF-036.rationale: The runner owns evidence storage and content-addressed artifact identity.

PERF-037.rationale: The provider declares completed JSON reports and the runner imports each report atomically.

PERF-038.rationale: The strict provider schema has no project-controlled output path.

PERF-039.rationale: Capability, category, metric, and report failures produce runner errors.

PERF-DEFECT-040.rationale: Separate purpose nodes and Axe ownership remove the one-run four-category coupling.
